result: I concluded that the methoxyphenyl group on N4 (ring C20–C25 plus O4/C32) is disordered, and I submitted a two-part model for it. In the original ordered model these atoms had very large, elongated displacement parameters (Ueq up to 0.19 Å², anisotropy ratios of 10–22). The strongest difference-map peaks, 1.8 and 1.6 e/Å³, all sat around O4, C32, C24, C23 and C22, while the rest of the molecule was well behaved. I modelled the group as two tilted orientations pivoting on N4, in PART 1 and PART 2. Their occupancies are tied to a free variable, which refined to 0.43/0.57. Each part has riding hydrogens, and the geometry is held by DFIX/SADI/FLAT restraints, with SIMU/RIGU on the displacements. Both parts are refined isotropically, and their Uiso values came out reasonable at 0.024–0.042 Å². R1 dropped from 0.0726 to 0.0600, wR2 from 0.243 to 0.191 and GooF from 1.60 to 1.25; the largest remaining peak is about 0.86 e/Å³, close to Cl3. My first attempt using rigid hexagons (AFIX 66) refined to a distorted ring, so I discarded it and rebuilt the parts with distance restraints. I left all other parts of the structure unchanged.
